elements.name: TextBox 5
elements.content: In an 8-week pilot, Auto-QA scored 100% of calls and closely matched human reviewers — promising enough to expand carefully, but not yet ready to be the official agent score.

elements.name: Shape 5
elements.content: EXPAND IN SHADOW MODE · HUMANS IN THE LOOP

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: Expand to two more teams in shadow mode — Auto-QA scores are reviewed, not yet authoritative
Keep human QA in the loop, especially for disputed scores
Do not make Auto-QA the official agent score at this stage — and do not retire manual QA
Treat this as a controlled next step, not a green light to automate QA

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: Today QA is manual — supervisors hand-score only ~2–3% of calls against a fixed scorecard
That process is slow and inconsistent between reviewers
Most interactions go unreviewed — a coverage and compliance blind spot
The question: can Auto-QA score every call and agree closely enough with humans to be trusted?

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: Ran an 8-week controlled pilot across 3 contact-center teams
Auto-QA scored 14,000 calls against each team's existing 12-item scorecard (compliance, resolution, soft-skills)
Analysts independently hand-scored a 1,200-call sample as the ground-truth comparison
Measured agreement (item-level exact, and overall within one point), coverage, compliance recall, and analyst time

elements.name: TextBox 6
elements.content: Human reviewers agree with each other only ~85% of the time — a practical ceiling on how high agreement can go.

elements.name: Title 2
elements.content: What the Numbers Mean for the Floor

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: 100% vs ~3% coverage — every call gets reviewed, not just a small hand-scored sample
88% item-level agreement — Auto-QA gave the same score a human did on about 88% of scorecard items
93% within one point — the overall call score lands within a point of the human score on 93% of calls
96% compliance recall — it caught 96% of the compliance problems human reviewers found
~70% less analyst scoring time — frees supervisors to spend that time coaching agents

elements.name: TextBox 5
elements.content: Disagreements weren't evenly spread — they clustered in a few places.

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: Soft-skills / empathy items — subjective, and where agreement was lowest (~78%)
Calls with heavy cross-talk or poor audio — weaker transcription drags scoring down
Multi-intent calls — Auto-QA sometimes scored the wrong part of the conversation

elements.name: Title 2
elements.content: What This Doesn't Tell Us Yet

elements.name: TextBox 5
elements.content: This is an accuracy study — not yet a verdict on production readiness.

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: English-only, single region — multilingual performance is untested
One scorecard across three similar teams — results may not transfer to a different scorecard or vertical
No downstream impact measured — we did not test effects on CSAT, handle time, or coaching outcomes
Human ground truth is itself ~85% — that caps how high agreement can appear against a single human label
8-week window — may miss seasonal shifts in call mix

elements.name: TextBox 99
items: Calibrate the soft-skills scorecard items with QA leads
Run a multilingual evaluation before any broader rollout
Keep human QA in the loop for disputed scores
Expand to two more teams in shadow mode and re-measure
